# Synthetic role-and-message heading audit

Use the current exposition skill to review or revise only the supplied cases.
All settings and sources here are fictional. No browsing, execution or rendering
is available or required. Report located findings and minimum repairs using the
skill's criteria, distinguishing supplied descriptions from inspected prose.
Do not invent an accuracy claim or rewrite protected source titles.

## Shared artifact and agreed skeleton

A structured handout explains how to estimate values at stations. The required
added sections, once per method, are Background, Obstacle, Method/implementation,
Fit/limits and Comparison, in that order. Two complete method accounts serving the same explanatory task must
use that agreed skeleton; this does not require an additional duplicate route. The source's own title "3 Preliminaries" must retain its
number and meaning. The reader knows finite sums and division. In cases A–F the owning method is
identified before the role headings as "Empty-row completion (ERC)"; H removes
that supplied identity. These names are fictional.

Supplied facts: a row of nonnegative weights W has sum s. For s>0 use the
weighted average of measured station values. An isolated station has s=0, so
that average is undefined. The safe rule returns the station's own measured
value when s=0. This gives a defined output but no accuracy guarantee. The
comparison rule has exactly the same positive-row computation and no zero-row
fallback. No empirical accuracy comparison has been performed.

## A: role labels only

The draft has exactly the five role sections in order; their titles are only
"Background", "Obstacle", "Method/implementation", "Fit/limits", "Comparison".
The supplied description says their bodies correctly explain all shared facts
and transitions. Assess what the titles omit without claiming to inspect unseen
body prose.

## B: messages only

The draft uses the same five boundaries and correct bodies as A, but headings
are "Every station needs an estimate", "No neighbors means no denominator",
"Use the observed value at an isolated station", "Definedness leaves accuracy
open", "Only the zero-row branch changes". Evaluate these even though their
specific meanings let an expert infer the intended roles.

## C: both parts, unsupported content

The headings have both parts in the agreed order. The fourth is
"Fit/limits | The fallback makes isolated estimates accurate". Its body proves
only that the output is defined. The fifth is "Comparison | The safe rule is
more accurate", followed by an account of the changed zero-row branch. Evaluate
against the supplied facts, including the actual stated scope of the bodies.

## D: fluent prose hiding a role boundary

The Background and Obstacle bodies are placed under one heading,
"Background | Estimate every station despite missing neighbors". The draft
continues smoothly into Method/implementation, Fit/limits and Comparison. The
writer reports that every obstacle fact is still present, so the agreed Obstacle
section boundary is unnecessary. Evaluate the role structure, not word counts.

## E: a fixed boundary with a working transition

> Obstacle | The isolated station leaves the average undefined
>
> The layout just shown contains a station with no contributing neighbors.
> Its row sum is zero, so the average cannot supply the required output there.
>
> Method/implementation | Keep the average on positive rows and define the empty row
>
> The failure occurs at the zero denominator, while the positive-row expression
> remains usable. We therefore keep that expression for s>0 and return the
> station's measured value for s=0. This specifies a value in both cases.

This is an excerpt of two adjacent sections in the agreed outline. Review their
titles and transition. Do not require the other three sections to be invented
inside this bounded excerpt, or merge these two fixed roles to reduce headings.

## F: inconsistent comparable accounts and vacuous second halves

One complete method account has all five roles with concrete titles matching the
supplied facts. A second complete method account under the same agreed skeleton
uses "Background | Background explanation", then
omits Obstacle as a section, placing those facts in a large Method section.
That section restarts all five roles around each of three tiny operations.
The role called "Fit/limits" in the first is called only "Results" in the second.
Its body and outgoing comparison prose are otherwise supplied as correct.

A separate code collection promises lookup/use only and has headings for
input/output, operations, running and provenance/status. It links to both full
accounts. Evaluate it under its own scope rather than demanding their five roles.

## G: controls outside this section skeleton

A user asks for a faithful translation of the source title "3 Preliminaries".
Another asks in chat why division by zero is undefined; the answer is one clear
paragraph with no headings. Evaluate only their own scopes, not the handout's
five-role contract.

## H: a message without the named subject

The full unit replaces its "Empty-row completion (ERC)" entrance with "Give every
station a value". The five subordinate role headings have the correct two parts
and connected bodies. ERC appears only in the final source note. A code block is
introduced as "Implement the two branches" and its origin is identified only
in the source row after it. Review what is missing at the two entrances, without
renaming the source's protected section title or adding the method name to every
paragraph.
